claim: The coordinated control of Ca2+ signaling is essential for development in eukaryotes.
source: The coordinated control of Ca2+ signaling is essential for development in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is a general statement about eukaryotic biology that draws from established scientific understanding.

claim: Cyclic nucleotide-gated channel (CNGC) family members mediate Ca2+ influx from cellular stores in plants.
source: Cyclic nucleotide-gated channel (CNGC) family members mediate Ca2+ influx from cellular stores in plants (Charpentier et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2016; Frietsch et al., 2007; Urquhart et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research studies.

claim: A quantitative gain-of-function CNGC mutation (brush) exists in Lotus japonicus.
source: Here, we report the unusual genetic behavior of a quantitative gain-of-function CNGC mutation (brush) in Lotus japonicus resulting in a leaky tetrameric channel.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the manuscript based on the research conducted.

claim: The brush mutation results in a leaky tetrameric channel.
source: Here, we report the unusual genetic behavior of a quantitative gain-of-function CNGC mutation (brush) in Lotus japonicus resulting in a leaky tetrameric channel.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental work described in the manuscript.

claim: brush resides in a cluster of redundant CNGCs encoding subunits.
source: brush resides in a cluster of redundant CNGCs encoding subunits which resemble metazoan voltage-gated potassium (Kv1-Kv4) channels in assembly and gating properties.
evidence: This is a finding from the genetic and molecular characterization performed in the study.

claim: The CNGC subunits in the brush cluster resemble metazoan voltage-gated potassium (Kv1-Kv4) channels in assembly and gating properties.
source: brush resides in a cluster of redundant CNGCs encoding subunits which resemble metazoan voltage-gated potassium (Kv1-Kv4) channels in assembly and gating properties.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis finding based on structural and functional characterization.

claim: The brush mutation is recessive and monogenic.
source: The recessive mongenic brush mutation impaired root development and infection by nitrogen-fixing rhizobia.
evidence: This is a genetic characterization finding from the study.

claim: The brush mutation impaired root development.
source: The recessive mongenic brush mutation impaired root development and infection by nitrogen-fixing rhizobia.
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from the experimental work.

claim: The brush mutation impaired infection by nitrogen-fixing rhizobia.
source: The recessive mongenic brush mutation impaired root development and infection by nitrogen-fixing rhizobia.
evidence: This is a phenotypic observation from nodulation experiments described in the methods.

claim: The brush allele exhibits quantitative behavior.
source: The brush allele exhibited quantitative behavior since overexpression of the cluster subunits was required to suppress the brush phenotype.
evidence: This is a finding from complementation experiments described in the study.

claim: Overexpression of the cluster subunits was required to suppress the brush phenotype.
source: The brush allele exhibited quantitative behavior since overexpression of the cluster subunits was required to suppress the brush phenotype.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from complementation studies.

claim: Quantitative competition between channel subunits for tetramer assembly can impact the phenotype of the mutation carrier.
source: The results reveal a mechanism by which quantitative competition between channel subunits for tetramer assembly can impact the phenotype of the mutation carrier.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Lotus japonicus Gifu is a wild-type accession (B-129).
source: Lotus japonicus Gifu (wild-type, accession B-129) (Handberg and Stougaard, 1992), Miyakojima (accession MG-20) (Kawaguchi et al., 2001) and brush (EMS mutant SL0979-2, Gifu) (Perry et al., 2003) plants were used.
evidence: This is a description of plant material used, supported by citation.

claim: Lotus japonicus Miyakojima is accession MG-20.
source: Lotus japonicus Gifu (wild-type, accession B-129) (Handberg and Stougaard, 1992), Miyakojima (accession MG-20) (Kawaguchi et al., 2001) and brush (EMS mutant SL0979-2, Gifu) (Perry et al., 2003) plants were used.
evidence: This is a description of plant material used, supported by citation.

claim: brush is an EMS mutant (SL0979-2) in the Gifu background.
source: Lotus japonicus Gifu (wild-type, accession B-129) (Handberg and Stougaard, 1992), Miyakojima (accession MG-20) (Kawaguchi et al., 2001) and brush (EMS mutant SL0979-2, Gifu) (Perry et al., 2003) plants were used.
evidence: This is a description of the mutant origin, supported by citation.

claim: The BRUSH TILLING line SL1484-1 was obtained from the L. japonicus TILLING facility at John Innes Centre, Norwich, UK.
source: The BRUSH TILLING line SL1484-1 was obtained from the L. japonicus TILLING facility (John Innes Centre, Norwich, UK).
evidence: This is a statement about the source of biological material.

claim: Hairy roots were generated using the Agrobacterium rhizogenes strain AR1193.
source: Hairy roots were generated using the Agrobacterium rhizogenes strain AR1193 (Stougaard et al., 1987).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: Nodulation experiments were carried out using Mesorhizobium loti MAFF303099 expressing DsRed.
source: Nodulation experiments were carried out by inoculating plants grown in pots or weck jars containing a sand-vermiculite mixture and Fåhraeus (Fahraeus, 1957) media with Mesorhizobium loti MAFF303099 expressing DsRed (Markmann et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citations.

claim: Plants were cultivated in growth cabinets at 22°C with 16 hr light/8 hr dark cycle.
source: Plants were cultivated in growth cabinets at 22°C (16 hr light/8 hr dark).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing growth conditions.

claim: All complementation and GUS experiments were carried out a minimum of three times and displayed similar results.
source: All complementation and GUS experiments were carried out a minimum of three times and displayed similar results.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental reproducibility.

claim: F2 plants from a cross between brush and MG-20 were used for fine mapping.
source: F2 plants from a cross between brush and MG-20 were used for fine mapping using SSR markers as described (Groth et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the mapping strategy, supported by citation.

claim: The brush target interval between TM2432 and SNP3 is approximately 103 kb.
source: The brush target interval between TM2432 and SNP3 (approximately 103 kb) was sequenced by Sanger sequencing.
evidence: This is a finding from the map-based cloning work.

claim: The brush genome was reassembled after next-generation sequencing to identify mutant-specific polymorphisms.
source: The brush genome was also reassembled after next-generation sequencing to identify mutant-specific polymorphisms.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the sequencing approach.

claim: Nuclear DNA of brush seedlings was subjected to next-generation sequencing using an Illumina HiSeq 2000 with a read length of 2 × 100 bp.
source: Nuclear DNA (see below) of brush seedlings was subjected to next-generation sequencing at Eurofins MWG, Germany, using an Illumina HiSeq 2000 (Illumina, USA) with a read length of 2 × 100 bp.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the sequencing parameters.

claim: Genes in the brush target region were annotated using Genscan and Artemis.
source: Genes in the brush target region were annotated after sequencing using Genscan (Burge and Karlin, 1997) and Artemis (Rutherford et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citations to the software tools.

claim: CLC Genomics Workbench was used to analyze the sequencing data.
source: CLC Genomics Workbench (CLC bio, Denmark) was used to analyze the sequencing data.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about data analysis.

claim: Yeast two-hybrid interaction assays were conducted with the haploid yeast strain AH109.
source: Yeast two-hybrid interaction assays were conducted with the haploid yeast strain AH109 (Clontech).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the yeast strain used.

claim: Split ubiquitin interaction assays were carried out in the haploid strain THY.AP4.
source: Split ubiquitin interaction assays were carried out in the haploid strain THY.AP4 (Obrdlik et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: The interacting protein pair of CCaMK and CYCLOPS was used as a control for yeast two-hybrid.
source: The interacting protein pair of CCaMK and CYCLOPS was used as a control for yeast two-hybrid (Yano et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about experimental controls, supported by citation.

claim: All interaction assays were independently conducted a minimum of three times.
source: All interaction assays were independently conducted a minimum of three times.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental reproducibility.

claim: BRUSH and brush coding sequences were cloned for Xenopus expression with a custom Golden Gate cloning strategy.
source: BRUSH and brush coding sequences were cloned for Xenopus expression with a custom Golden Gate cloning strategy using a modified backbone obtained from the Standard European Vector Architecture 2.0 database (Martinez-Garcia et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: The backbone was derived from pSEVA191 and was chosen to alleviate toxicity issues uncovered while cloning CNGC.IVA sequences into pUC-based Golden Gate backbones and pGEMHE.
source: The backbone (with flanking bacterial transcriptional terminators) was derived from pSEVA191 (http://wwwuser.cnb.csic.es/~seva/) and was chosen to alleviate toxicity issues uncovered while cloning CNGC.IVA sequences into pUC-based Golden Gate backbones and pGEMHE (Liman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is a methodological statement explaining the rationale for vector choice, supported by citation.

claim: cRNA was synthesized with a mMESSAGE mMACHINE T7 Transcription Kit.
source: cRNA was synthesized with a mMESSAGE mMACHINE T7 Transcription Kit (ThermoFisher, Germany) and oocytes were injected (General Valve Picospritzer III, Parker Hannifin Corp.) with approximately 25 ng cRNA or with RNase-free water as a control.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental procedure.

claim: Oocytes were injected with approximately 25 ng cRNA or with RNase-free water as a control.
source: cRNA was synthesized with a mMESSAGE mMACHINE T7 Transcription Kit (ThermoFisher, Germany) and oocytes were injected (General Valve Picospritzer III, Parker Hannifin Corp.) with approximately 25 ng cRNA or with RNase-free water as a control.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental procedure.

claim: Injected oocytes were stored at 18°C in ND96 solution.
source: Injected oocytes were stored at 18°C in ND96 solution (96 mM NaCl, 2 mM KCl, 1 mM CaCl2, 1 mM MgCl2, 5 mM HEPES, 10 mM sorbitol, pH 7.4 with NaOH) adjusted to 220 mOsm/L with sorbitol and supplemented with 25 µg/ml gentamycin until use.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing storage conditions.

claim: Measurements were recorded 2 to 3 days after injection using the two-electrode voltage-clamp technique.
source: Measurements were recorded 2 to 3 days after injection using the two-electrode voltage-clamp technique with a Turbo Tec-10Cx amplifier (NPI electronic GmbH).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the recording procedure.

claim: During two-electrode voltage clamp measurements, oocytes were constantly perfused with bath solution composed of 30 mM CaCl2, 10 mM MES-Tris pH 7.4, adjusted to 220 mOsm/L with mannitol and supplemented with either 100 µM 8-Bromo-cAMP or 100 µM 8-CPT-cAMP.
source: During two-electrode voltage clamp measurements, oocytes were constantly perfused with bath solution composed of 30 mM CaCl2, 10 mM MES-Tris pH 7.4, adjusted to 220 mOsm/L with mannitol and supplemented with either 100 µM 8-Bromo-cAMP (Sigma) or 100 µM 8-CPT-cAMP (BioLog).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing experimental conditions.

claim: Voltage steps from +60 to −160 mV in 20 mV increments were applied starting from a holding potential of −40 mV.
source: Starting from a holding potential of −40 mV, voltage steps from +60 to −160 mV in 20 mV increments were applied (PatchMaster, HEKA Electronics Inc.).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the voltage-clamp protocol.

claim: Oocytes were imaged by confocal microscopy 2 to 3 days after injection with BRUSH-YFP and brush-YFP cRNA to confirm expression.
source: Oocytes were imaged by confocal microscopy 2 to 3 days after injection with BRUSH-YFP and brush-YFP cRNA (Leica TCS SP5, excitation: 488 nm, detection: 525–575 nm) to confirm expression.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the imaging procedure.

claim: For BiFC experiments, cRNAs were mixed 1:1 prior to injection.
source: The same protocol was used for BiFC experiments, except that cRNAs were mixed 1:1 prior to injection.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the BiFC experimental procedure.

claim: Lotus japonicus Gifu seeds were germinated and grown on half-strength B5 agar plates for 14 days for gene expression analysis after rhizobial inoculation.
source: For analysis of gene expression after rhizobial inoculation, Lotus japonicus Gifu seeds were germinated and grown on half-strength B5 agar plates for 14 days.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental setup.

claim: Six plants were planted per weck jar containing sand/vermiculite with Fåhraeus media for gene expression analysis.
source: Six plants were planted per weck jar containing sand/vermiculite with Fåhraeus media.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental setup.

claim: Root tissue from a single jar was collected and pooled to represent a biological replicate.
source: After 7 days, root tissue from a single jar was collected and pooled (represents a biological replicate) for the Day 0 time point.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the sampling strategy.

claim: Positive hairy roots were isolated from individual plants 6 weeks after inoculation with Mesorhizobium loti MAFF303099 DsRed for RNAi gene expression analysis.
source: To analyze gene expression after RNAi, positive hairy roots were isolated from individual plants 6 weeks after inoculation with Mesorhizobium loti MAFF303099 DsRed.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental procedure.

claim: RNA was extracted with a Spectrum Plant Total RNA Kit.
source: For both experiments, root tissue was ground in liquid nitrogen and RNA was extracted with a Spectrum Plant Total RNA Kit (Sigma).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the RNA extraction procedure.

claim: Genomic DNA was removed using a Turbo DNA-free Kit.
source: Genomic DNA was removed using a Turbo DNA-free Kit (Ambion) and total RNA (1 μg for the time course and 200 ng for RNAi) was used for cDNA synthesis with Superscript III (ThermoFisher).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the RNA processing procedure.

claim: 1 μg total RNA was used for cDNA synthesis for the time course experiment and 200 ng for RNAi.
source: Genomic DNA was removed using a Turbo DNA-free Kit (Ambion) and total RNA (1 μg for the time course and 200 ng for RNAi) was used for cDNA synthesis with Superscript III (ThermoFisher).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the cDNA synthesis procedure.

claim: cDNA was checked for genomic DNA contamination by PCR.
source: cDNA was then checked for genomic DNA contamination by PCR.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing quality control procedures.

claim: Expression of CNGC.IVA cluster genes after rhizobia inoculation was analyzed by qPCR using SYBR Select Master Mix with a CFX96 real-time PCR machine.
source: Expression of CNGC.IVA cluster genes after rhizobia inoculation was analyzed by qPCR using SYBR Select Master Mix (Applied Biosystems) with a CFX96 real-time PCR machine.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the qPCR procedure.

claim: brush expression after RNAi was analyzed by qPCR using mi-real-time EvaGreen Master Mix with a QuantStudio 5 Real-Time PCR System.
source: brush expression after RNAi was analyzed by qPCR using mi-real-time EvaGreen Master Mix (Metabion) with a QuantStudio 5 Real-Time PCR System (ThermoFisher).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the qPCR procedure.

claim: The plotted data point for each biological replicate represents the mean of three technical replicates.
source: In both cases, the plotted data point for each biological replicate represents the mean of three technical replicates.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing data representation.

claim: The relative expression was calculated with the 2-ΔΔCT method using eEF-1Aα as the reference.
source: The relative expression was calculated with the 2-ΔΔCT method (Schmittgen and Livak, 2008) using eEF-1Aα (GenBank: BP045727) as the reference.
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: Arabidopsis thaliana protein sequences were obtained from The Arabidopsis Information Resource (TAIR).
source: Arabidopsis thaliana protein sequences were obtained from The Arabidopsis Information Resource (TAIR).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the data source.

claim: A multiple sequence alignment was generated using MUSCLE in CLC Main Workbench.
source: A multiple sequence alignment was generated using MUSCLE in CLC Main Workbench (CLC bio, Denmark).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the bioinformatics analysis.

claim: A Maximum Likelihood phylogenetic tree was calculated using UPGMA with 100 bootstrap iterations.
source: A Maximum Likelihood phylogenetic tree was calculated using UPGMA (100 bootstrap iterations were performed).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the phylogenetic analysis.

claim: One-way ANOVA statistical analysis followed by a post-hoc Tukey's multiple comparisons test and t-tests were calculated using GraphPad Prism.
source: One-way ANOVA statistical analysis of data followed by a post-hoc Tukey's multiple comparisons test and t-tests were calculated using GraphPad Prism.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the statistical analysis.
